operation_details.item: The user has a nickel allergy and must avoid direct skin contact with nickel-containing metals.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good afternoon! How was your coding session today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It was productive, but I’m thinking about getting a new watch for long coding hours. My current one is uncomfortable.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A watch can be a great tool for keeping track of time during deep work. What kind of band are you considering?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m not sure about the band. I’ve had issues with metal bands in the past—they tend to irritate my skin.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Skin irritation from metal bands is often linked to nickel content. Do you have a known sensitivity to nickel?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I have a nickel allergy; wearing metal watch bands, belt buckles, or jewelry causes skin irritation.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. For a watch, you’ll want to avoid nickel-containing metals. Look for bands made of titanium, ceramic, or stainless steel that is labeled nickel-free. Leather, silicone, or fabric bands are also safe options.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks! Are there specific materials or brands you recommend that are known to be hypoallergenic?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Titanium is a great hypoallergenic metal. For non-metal options, consider a high-quality leather band or a woven nylon strap. Many watchmakers now list nickel-free or hypoallergenic specs in their product details.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That’s helpful. I’ll also check the metal composition of any watch I consider. Is there a standard way to verify it?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: You can look for certifications like "nickel-free" or "hypoallergenic" on the packaging. Some manufacturers provide material composition details online. For metals, surgical-grade stainless steel (316L) is often low in nickel, but titanium is your safest bet.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Perfect, I’ll keep that in mind. Thanks for the advice—I think I’ll go with a titanium band watch.
